description: F-CORE-032: partner master data can be entered correctly and corrected afterwards. Four gaps that only add up once a screen maintains partners, and an embedding application hit all four. (1) `createPartner` documented every field as optional and defaulted `name` to the empty string, so a request that forgot the name created a nameless partner indistinguishable from the next one — the app ended up refusing it in its own route, which is the wrong place: master data that is wrong here is wrong for every reader of the books. (2) `kind` was a plain string, so `custommer` was a partner kind like any other and only surfaced as a category nothing could filter on; the manual has named `customer`/`supplier`/`both` all along. (3) `accountNumbers` and `address` were create-only, so a wrong account link was permanent — the partner had to be abandoned and recreated under a new id while every open item stayed on the old one. (4) `paymentTermsDays` could be set and never cleared, because it was read with a number check while `vatId` accepted `null` to clear: two fields, two behaviours, nothing saying so. Deliberately still absent: `deletePartner`. Books keep what they referenced, and an id that open items point at must not vanish.

expect.comment: No name. Before this it created a partner called "" — findable by id and by nothing else.
Whitespace is not a name either. A form that trims nothing must not pass one through.
The near miss. The three kinds are customer, supplier and both — anything else used to be stored as given.
The correction that was impossible: the account link moves, and so does the address. Both replace wholesale — 'these are the accounts now' is what a form can state.
Clearing the term, the way vatId: null has always cleared the VAT id. Before this the field simply kept its old value and the answer looked like a success.
A name cannot be cleared either — absent leaves it alone, present and empty is the same mistake as creating without one.

Every accepted change is in the trail as a before/after diff, and the refused ones are not — a rejection must leave nothing behind. The cleared payment term shows as `to: null`, which is what makes 'cleared' distinguishable from 'never set' when reading the history back.
